pages.text: "I am fastest!" Impatient Bobo hopped onto a tricycle. One front-wheel track crossed the dirt yard. Bobo pulled the purple hat brim forward.
"I will reach that tree in a blink!" Bobo pedaled without stopping. Rattle, rattle—across the yard, Teacher Bau watered pots.
The tricycle sped across the yard. Bobo watched only their feet and pedaled more. The wheel track curved and twisted.
Gaga, who knew best, stretched their neck to watch. "Bobo, that is not how to ride." Bobo pretended not to hear and pedaled faster.
Gaga put both hands on their hips. "Feet slow, eyes ahead! That is how to ride!" "I like fast!" Bobo sped on.
Suddenly, the water-play tub appeared ahead. Crash! The front wheel hit it; the tricycle tipped. Bobo quickly planted both feet on the ground.
Water spilled, soaking the yard. The tricycle lay on its side, wheels spinning uselessly. "I did not even reach the tree..." Bobo's shoulders drooped.
Teacher Bau came and stood the tricycle up. Then a finger slowly traced its track in the dirt: twisting curves that stopped at the tub.
Bobo climbed on again. "One, feet slow! Two, eyes ahead! Three, if something is ahead, foot down!" At the tub, Bobo planted a foot and stopped. Feet slow, eyes ahead!
Bobo circled the yard and stopped at the tree. Teacher Bau lifted Bobo off the tricycle. Going slowly gets you where you want to go. "Gaga, did you see? Feet slow, eyes ahead!"
